# Refactoring Code and Why You Should Do It

## A Working Code Does Not Mean It Is Good
Lets say you put in a few hours into building code for a website and did not take into account of others reading the code at a later date. Those people will have no clue on what your x, y, or z will even mean and that is where refactoring comes in. Once you are finished building your code look back at it an check to see if it is easliy readable and understandable on what each component does not just for you but for those who come after.

## Why Refactor?
Not everything is portrayed clearly across all developers and that is why you refactor to reach a sort of mid point of understanding between everyone. One of the big points of refactoring is that it makes code easier to read. It also helps make code more bug free and compound. Trust me, if you plan to maintain a website without refactoring you are in for a bumpy ride.

## What are Coding Smells?
To put it simply it is a method to figure out what needs to be refactored in a piece of code. 
These are examples of code smell:
- Long Method
- Magic Number and Strings
- Duplicated Code
- Poor Naming
- Long Parameter List
- Large Class/God Object
- Feature Envy
- Comments that Apologize

These are the Code smells that are most known, if you wish to know more I encourage you to look at it more in depth from someone who is more knowledgable about it.
